strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with interleaved scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with local scale/unscale operations between each pair, exactly as in the reference implementation. Dispatch count: 8 all-reduces + 14 local element-wise ops = 22 dispatches. Represents the baseline: maximum correctness clarity, no fusion, highest dispatch overhead.

strategies.name: Fused local operations between all-reduces
strategies.desc: Keeps 8 all-reduce operations but fuses all scale, multiply, and divide operations into single kernels between collective calls. Dispatch count: 8 all-reduces + 7 fused local kernels = 15 dispatches. Trades kernel fusion complexity for ~30% fewer dispatches by batching element-wise operations.

strategies.name: Precompute scaling patterns, vectorized shard ops
strategies.desc: Precomputes the compound scaling factors (a[r]/W applied 8 times with intervening divisions) outside the main loop, then performs all-reduces with a single vectorized scaling operation per stage. Dispatch count: 8 all-reduces + 8 vectorized scale ops + 1 precompute = 17 dispatches. Reduces per-shard indexing overhead by treating the full vector uniformly.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter and all-gather decomposition
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing computation overlap during the gather phase (each rank can start local operations on its reduced shard immediately). Dispatch count: 8×2 = 16 collectives + 7 overlapped local ops = 23 dispatches. Trades more collectives for potential pipeline parallelism and reduced per-collective payload size.

strategies.name: Hierarchical reduction with pre-scaled buffers
strategies.desc:
Pre-allocates and pre-scales multiple buffers simultaneously, then chains all-reduces with buffer swapping instead of in-place modification. Uses double-buffering to allow async launch of next all-reduce while previous completes. Dispatch count: 8 all-reduces + 1 batch buffer preparation + 7 buffer swaps = 16 dispatches. Hides latency through pipelining at cost of 2× memory footprint.
